title: The H Heuristics November 12th Update
subtitle: Strategy, Scenarios, and the Operational Transition from Concept Genesis to Global Adoption
description: Documents the 12 November 2026 shift from publishing concepts to disseminating and testing them: the person-years finding, a five-stage adoption plan and Bass diffusion scenarios.
contribution: Records the strategic pivot to adoption and the five publications that carried it, and sets out the adoption plan, scenario assumptions, risk register and 2026–2050 roadmap, with its own limits stated.
abstract: On 12 November 2026, H Heuristics shifted its mission from developing and publishing concepts to also disseminating, testing, and applying them. This report documents that pivot and the five coordinated publications that carried it out: Century Pathways (HH-2026-61), The Macroeconomic Architecture (HH-2026-62), the Global Concept Adoption Initiative (HH-2026-63), and two companion Substack essays, supported by Positive Pathways (HH-2026-60) and synthesized in The November 2026 Update (HH-2026-64).

The pivot rests on a three-step chain: ideas influence decisions, decisions direct investment, and investment changes development trajectories. The empirical anchor is the person-years metric. If access to five basic services (electricity, clean cooking, broadband, piped water, sanitation) stayed frozen at 2025 levels, cumulative deprivation over 2026–2100 would reach 859 billion person-years. At proven peer-pace rollout it falls to 112 billion, a 143 billion person-year gap against the 255 billion current-trend trajectory. The Decoupling Proposition argues that human welfare can improve while planetary hazards rise, provided vulnerability falls faster than hazards grow.

The operating plan has four parts: a five-stage theory of change (Develop, Disseminate, Adopt, Apply, Improve) with closed-loop feedback; a network of about 100 Anchor Experts, reached through personalized, CAN-SPAM- and GDPR-compliant outreach; a Bass diffusion scenario projecting roughly 140 independent citations by 2030, 670 by 2035, and 2,900 by 2050 (envelope 1,100–7,900), with only third-party citations counted; and a Two-Channel Engine pairing a top-down institutional channel, capped at 10% adoption, with an unbounded open-web channel.

The report is explicit about its limits. The Bass parameters (p = 0.015, q = 0.28) are assumed rather than calibrated, the institutional ratios are fixed rather than modeled, and the outreach claims are self-reported. It also contrasts the assertive framing of HH-62 with the more cautious “proposed frameworks” framing of HH-63/64, and it closes with a risk register and a 2026–2050 roadmap beginning with a 12-month Clean Cooking Sprint and a first annual audit in November 2027.
coreProposition: Ideas can influence decisions, decisions can direct investment, and investment can change development trajectories, so intellectual influence is treated as an active, measurable instrument of development.

keyFindings.title: From publishing to adoption.
keyFindings.text: On 12 November 2026 H Heuristics moved from mainly formulating concepts to also spreading, testing and applying them, through five coordinated publications spanning theory, empirical data and operations.

keyFindings.title: The person-years finding.
keyFindings.text: With access to five basic services frozen at 2025 levels, cumulative deprivation over 2026–2100 reaches 859 billion person-years; at proven peer-pace rollout it falls to 112 billion, against 255 billion on current trend, a 143 billion person-year gap.

keyFindings.title: The Decoupling Proposition.
keyFindings.text: Human welfare can improve even as planetary hazards escalate, provided infrastructure deployment cuts vulnerability faster than hazards grow: risk sets the deadline, development sets the outcome.

keyFindings.title: A five-stage plan and an anchor network.
keyFindings.text: A theory of change running Develop, Disseminate, Adopt, Apply, Improve, with four participant roles and about 100 Anchor Experts reached by personalized, rule-compliant outreach.

keyFindings.title: Citation scenarios, not forecasts.
keyFindings.text: A Bass diffusion scenario projects about 140 independent citations by 2030, 670 by 2035 and 2,900 by 2050 (envelope 1,100–7,900; no-outreach counterfactual 500), with 148,000 readers, using assumed parameters (p = 0.015, q = 0.28) and fixed institutional ratios.

keyFindings.title: Stated limits and a recalibration.
keyFindings.text: The report acknowledges that the parameters are assumed, the outreach claims are self-reported, and the earlier HH-62 projection (3,800 citations, 290,000 readers) was more assertive than the 2,900 and 148,000 used here.

keyFindings.title: A two-channel engine.
keyFindings.text: A top-down institutional channel capped at 10% adoption is paired with an unbounded decentralized open-web channel, so reach does not depend on bureaucratic uptake.

keyFindings.title: Roadmap and audit.
keyFindings.text: A 12-month Clean Cooking Sprint and a first annual adoption audit in November 2027 open a four-phase roadmap (Seeding, Validation, Institutionalization, Convergence) running to 2050 and beyond.

bottomLine: A strategy-and-scenarios report on turning published concepts into adopted ones. Its citation and reader figures are assumed-parameter scenarios, its outreach claims are self-reported, and its case studies are illustrative rather than sourced evidence.

glossary.term: Intellectual Influence as an Instrument of Development
glossary.definition: The doctrine that economic research should actively direct sovereign and multilateral capital toward preventive civil defense rather than remain passive analysis.
Ideas influence decisions; decisions direct investment; investment changes development trajectories.
The cumulative number of unserved people multiplied by the duration of their deprivation across electricity, clean cooking, broadband, piped water and sanitation.
The counterfactual in which the share of the global population with basic service access stays at 2025 levels through 2100 (859 billion person-years).
The infrastructure delivery speed already demonstrated by peer developing nations, applied across unserved regions.
The difference between the 255 billion person-year current-trend trajectory and the 112 billion person-year peer-pace trajectory.
The proposition that human welfare can be decoupled from environmental breakdown if infrastructure deployment cuts vulnerability faster than hazards grow.
The governance pipeline unifying six concepts into diagnosis (Polycrisis Resilience, HVRE), execution (PDE, Sustainable Convergence) and valuation (Development Optimization, HSD).
An economic framework that defines wealth through the security and dignity guaranteed to human biology, auditing six endowments across four exposure arenas.
The adoption model in HH-63: Develop (open research), Disseminate (targeted briefs), Adopt (syllabi and policies), Apply (physical capital), Improve (empirical feedback).
A curated network of high-credibility scholars, modelers and technocrats whose early adoption is intended to create pull across the wider field.
A top-down institutional channel capped at 10% paired with an unbounded decentralized open-web channel.
Presenting frameworks as testable hypotheses and labeling projections as scenarios rather than forecasts.
Counting only third-party, non-self citations in peer-reviewed journals, dissertations and official policy acts.
The first-year thematic campaign engaging public health and energy ministries on the clean-cooking deficit through electric induction cooking.
The mid-century aim that every person is shielded by modern civil-defense infrastructure within safe planetary boundaries.
